reference_contract:
Original industrial exploration spacecraft, based only on the small STARTER ship marked 01 at the BOTTOM LEFT of the reference. This is a sample assembly of a freely configurable module kit, NOT a fixed mandatory upgrade path for all players. Keep its distinctive sharply sloping wedge cockpit with wraparound segmented dark glass, low rectangular central spine, paired short cylindrical rear engine pods, ivory ceramic-alloy armor over graphite structure, and restrained ochre service panels. Starter is compact, has no crane, no giant jump ring, no living greenhouse, no hangar, no large solar wings. Show simple purposeful surfaces and credible separate parts, with clean legible interfaces and restrained fine detail.
Assembly contract: one C01 wedge cockpit at the nose; repeated S01 short rectangular keel segments along the centerline; one J01 four-way structural junction within the keel; one H01 low rectangular power/service body behind the cockpit; two G01 removable rectangular cargo pods, one on each side; two identical P01 cylindrical engine pods supported by two A01 mechanical pylons at the rear, with two rear-facing main exhaust openings total; K01 removable outer fairings and blanking caps. Common large square chamfer-corner structural coupling is used by keel/junction/cockpit/service parts; separate smaller keyed mechanical hardpoints hold equipment/pylons. Standardized interfaces permit length extension, lateral branches, optional asymmetry and independent engine relocation using adapters. Precisely two engine pods and one cockpit in the baseline. A small non-glowing rectangular maintenance access panel on the STARBOARD cargo pod distinguishes port and starboard; retain its location in every view. This contract defines intended geometry for human modeling reference, not production-verified CAD.

Layout: a clean professional high-resolution landscape sheet on a uniform light neutral gray background. Exactly SIX generously separated panels in a 2-column by 3-row layout. Top row: FRONT on left, BACK on right. Middle row: LEFT on left, RIGHT on right. Bottom row: TOP on left, BOTTOM on right.
Each panel contains exactly ONE fully assembled baseline ship in a true straight-on orthographic projection. FRONT is looking at the nose, BACK shows both engine exhausts; LEFT is the port side profile with the nose pointing LEFT; RIGHT is the starboard side profile with the nose pointing RIGHT; TOP is a straight overhead plan with nose pointing UP; BOTTOM is the underside plan with nose pointing UP. No perspective three-quarter views on this sheet.
All views describe exactly the same object: same cockpit window subdivisions, armor breaks, connection flanges, two cargo pods and two engine pods, same relative sizes and materials. Maintain a coherent orthographic shape across all panels. Do not redesign any view. Center every ship with ample blank margins; no cropping and no overlap. Use uniform soft studio illumination, clear surfaces and edges, no cast floor shadows, no engine glow, no depth of field, no scenery, no grid, no dimension arrows or measurement claims.
Text: small plain labels exactly "FRONT", "BACK", "LEFT", "RIGHT", "TOP", "BOTTOM" under their respective views. No other text or decorative interface. High-end hard-surface concept reference quality, convincing but restrained material response. Clear modular seams.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: modular spaceship exploded-view design reference.
Input image 1 is the approved six-view reference of the assembled starter sample. Preserve its actual hull proportions, wedge cockpit, twin cylindrical engines, rectangular cargo pods and industrial material language.
Primary request: create one polished landscape modular breakdown sheet explaining how this starter assembly is built from REUSABLE, REARRANGEABLE parts. The user needs broad player customization; the ship is just one layout from a kit.
Style: crisp premium hard-surface product rendering on a light neutral studio background, softly illuminated, no dramatic shadows, no stars, no glow, no vignette. Engineering legibility and distinctive silhouettes.
Composition: upper two-thirds one large clean axonometric EXPLODED assembly, nose toward lower-left and engine end toward upper-right. Clearly separate the cockpit, central frame segments, utility body, side cargo pods, rear pylons, engine pods, and outer covers along logical assembly directions. Fine neutral exploded leader lines should show where components attach, without crossing important silhouettes. Include one small intact starter ship inset for comparison. Every physical part is fully visible, with clear negative space.
The reusable part types are exactly: C01 wedge cockpit; S01 short straight rectangular keel segment; J01 four-way structural junction; H01 low rectangular power/service body; G01 rectangular cargo pod; P01 one cylindrical engine pod (two identical copies in the starter); A01 engine/equipment pylon (two copies in the starter); K01 fairing and blanking-cap set.
Expose mating faces that make sense. C01/S01/J01/H01 share a consistent LARGE CHAMFER-CORNER SQUARE structural flange called U1. Equipment uses a consistent smaller keyed mount called U2. Show U1 as square bulkhead attachment and U2 as mechanical attachment; do not make these two interfaces look identical. The J01 junction must visibly support lateral branches as well as fore/aft extension. S01 segments are repeatable; engine pylons and cargo modules are relocatable through matching mounts. The centerline is extensible and can branch, rather than a single unchangeable chassis.
Bottom third: exactly eight clean isolated part thumbnails with readable labels ONLY "C01", "S01", "J01", "H01", "G01", "P01", "A01", "K01", one of each category. The exploded assembly uses the same IDs with restrained leaders, no prose. Two small interface close-ups may be labeled only "U1" and "U2".
Do not show upgrade stages or fixed classes. No dimension numbers, unverified measurements, branding or watermark. This is an art/modeling breakdown, not certified CAD. Match the supplied starter exterior; internal frames are functional concept design to support that exterior.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: player-built modular spaceship silhouette comparison.
Input image 1 is the starter kit design reference. Use its wedge cockpit, ceramic-alloy and graphite materials, ochre service panels, rectangular detachable cargo pods, standardized short frame sections, cylindrical engine pods, and visible attachment style.
Primary request: demonstrate that different players using a SHARED modular kit can create ships with OBVIOUSLY DIFFERENT OVERALL SHAPES. These are peer-level layout examples, NOT successive upgrades and NOT locked professions. Keep the SAME material palette across all three so their difference is caused by geometry rather than paint.
A clean high-end landscape concept sheet on uniform light neutral background, exactly three generous separate columns, one assembled spacecraft per column, full three-quarter orthographic product view from above-front-left. All three ships have the same distinctive starter wedge cockpit and the same two cylindrical engine models, with reused recognizable cargo pod models. Keep cockpit size comparable across the columns; fit all geometry without clipping. Excellent believable hard-surface materials, simple legible structural connections, no space backdrop.
LEFT / label "LONG": a narrow elongated ship with repeated keel segments, slim single central body, two engines closely grouped at the rear, minimal side cargo. Its silhouette should be unmistakably a long dart.
CENTER / label "WIDE": a short broad ship constructed around branching cross-junctions, four rectangular cargo pods in a wide twin-bank arrangement, engines placed outboard on matching pylons, cockpit on the forward middle branch. Its silhouette should be unmistakably a compact wide freighter.
RIGHT / label "OFFSET": a distinctive asymmetric ship. The SAME cockpit mounts forward on the left branch of a cross-junction, a row of reused cargo pods runs aft along the right branch, connected by a visible transverse structural bridge. Place two reused engine pods on suitable rear pylons. The silhouette has a deliberate offset nose and negative space between the branches, structurally credible rather than a random floating collage.
Each craft should visibly be built from repeated interchangeable parts. Use extra frame/junction segments and rearrangement to explain the different footprint. Do not add fancy exclusive engines, huge rings, weapons, cranes or greenhouse modules. No arrows between columns, no progression numbers, no power comparisons.
Text only "LONG", "WIDE", "OFFSET", one label under each ship. No other text.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: a SINGLE isolated directional reference image for Tripo multi-view modeling.
Input image 1 is the approved six-view starter ship sheet and is the EDIT TARGET.
Primary request: isolate ONLY the ship in the TOP-LEFT panel labeled FRONT into a standalone high-resolution image. This is a faithful panel extraction and clean enlargement, not a redesign.
Exact view: looking straight at the nose. Two circular FRONT engine caps flank the upper body; the faceted cockpit windshield is centered lower down.
Keep the reference ship's geometry, silhouette, window subdivisions, existing panel seams, cargo pod placements, paired-engine configuration, material colors, viewpoint and orthographic projection unchanged. Show only surfaces already visible in that selected panel. Do not infer a different camera angle, add parts, simplify the shape, add perspective, switch left/right, or use any other panel.
Remove all panel boundaries and text labels. Center the complete ship on a uniform light neutral gray studio background with comfortable margins on every side. One ship, one view, no captions, no diagram, no collage, no ground-plane cast shadows, no engine glow or atmospheric effects. Clean edges and readable structure for modeling; no cropping. Preserve the whole silhouette exactly. For a side elevation use a landscape composition to keep the ship large; for front/back use a square composition. All imagery should match the supplied reference rather than a newly imagined ship.
